messages:
alex: @oncall getting paged — sudden rise in 429 errors on /v1/generate (hosted). Dash: https://dash.internal/redwood/429-trends :rotating_light:
incident-bot: ALERT 1920456789 — 429-rate > 15% sustained for 3m across region-us-east-1. Triggered paging to eng-oncall.
sre-monitor: quick metric snapshot — p95 latency +1.2s, request rate steady, error-rate spike concentrated on tenant-ids: tenant-alpha, tenant-gamma, tenant-legacy.
priya: copying graphs. looks correlated with the new batching rollout (batcher v2) -> qt: sequence length increase?
noah: grabbing traces. initial look: many 429s originate from the routing layer returning early when queue depth hits per-tenant QPS cap.
jamie: can we open a surgical cap on the noisy tenants while we investigate? prefer not to throttle globally.
alex: agreed. plan: 1) apply temporary per-tenant QPS caps for top offenders 2) disable noncritical pre-processing hooks for hosted mode 3) monitor 429/503 trends for 15m and reassess.
priya: prepared a CLI snippet to set caps:
```bash
# apply tenant cap via infractl
infractl ratecap set --tenant tenant-alpha --qps 20 --reason "live mitigation 429 spike"
infractl ratecap set --tenant tenant-gamma --qps 15 --reason "live mitigation 429 spike"
```
noah: running now for tenant-alpha -> response: OK 202. applying to tenant-gamma..
incident-bot: ACTION logged — ratecap change by noah at 1920456823.
noah: tenant-gamma OK. both caps in place.
jamie: disabling preproc hooks (spellcheck/training-signal) for hosted in us-east-1. command: `service toggle preproc --env hosted --region us-east-1 --component spellcheck --off`
priya: done for spellcheck, training-signal queued and off in 10s.
sre-monitor: dashboard query used: `sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"4..",path="/v1/generate"}[1m])) by (tenant, status)` — showing 429 drop from 18% -> 8% within 2m after caps. 503 stable ~0.6% 
noah: small increase in p50 latency for capped tenants (requests being queued client-side), but 429s reduced. customer impact: alpha and gamma degraded but not fully blocked.
alex: notifying customer-success: @ops-leads FYI we've applied surgical caps to reduce cascading 429s. This may increase tail latency for those tenants. message suggested: "We've applied temporary throughput limits to avoid broader outage; we're monitoring and will update every 15m."
ops-leads: acknowledged, will prepare PSR if it persists.
jamie: can we enable model-fallback for heavy requests to reduce CPU on the main model? toggle via route fallback policy to model-small for requests over 8k tokens.
priya: creating canary fallback: `routerctl set-fallback --route /v1/generate --condition token_length>8000 --fallback small-model-v1 --duration 30m`
noah: applied canary fallback 1% traffic -> no significant quality complaints in logs. metrics: fallback hit 0.4% so far.
sre-monitor: keep watching 503s. any 503s appear are from upstream model-server OOMs. mitigation: scale dedicated pool if OOMs increase.
alex: next steps timeline: 1) monitor 15m windows 2) if 429s <5% continue to uplift caps slowly 3) if 503s >1% initiate pool scale + alert infra.
jamie: handoff note — i'm on until 22:30 UTC, then @jamie -> @noah will take over. leaving a runbook snippet in thread.
noah: taking over at 22:30 UTC. will watch dashboards and follow same escalation.
priya: flagging one tenant (tenant-legacy) with repeated 429s — consider a targeted migration or quota bump after we stabilize. opened ticket: https://tracker.internal/TKT-4982
alex: customer impact summary for oncall notes: affected tenants: tenant-alpha, tenant-gamma, tenant-legacy. mitigation actions: per-tenant caps, disabled preproc hooks, canary model fallback. status: stabilizing, 429s down ~55% from peak, 503s unchanged.
incident-bot: UPDATE 1920456920 — 429-rate trending downward. Next automated check at +15m.
noah: logging final observation before handoff: keep caps in place until we see two clean 5m windows. if client complaints grow, coordinate with CS for temporary credits.
jamie: :thumbsup: leaving notes in pagerduty.
alex: thanks team — we'll keep this thread as the single source of truth during mitigation. I'll update if we need escalation to infra.
noah: signing off for handoff (watching alerts).
